Kenzo: What's the what's the most important things to know about them?
DM: Is clearly like super nervous. I am taking a huge risk, trusting you.
Wellby: You're asking us to take a huge risk. It goes both ways.
DM: Rodnya Kinzal, has never cared much for the people of Ursk, is negotiating a peace deal with Rhodar von Glauer that I am sure will include regular sacrifices to feed his growing vampire armies.

DM: We cannot stop this, not right now, anyway, and Branek does not intend to stop— cares only about keeping the secret elemental knowledge of our order alive and resurrecting his dear leader, got us into this mess in the first place. There’s a reason this magic is forbidden, and if he had— well, if he would cooperate, that dragon could have been killed in other ways.

DM: There is a group of us. Cannot tell you who. Because if you don't— listen, you don't care, all I can do is vanish silently into the night, and hope that if you say anything to Branek, he ignores you, or treats you as foolish, or doesn't believe you, or perhaps that you won't say anything to him.
DM: There is a group of us that is prepared to lay claim to the Rodnya Voknaz bloodline, and reposition ourselves as the guardians of the people of Ursk, and stop this deal.

DM: Do not believe the other Rodnya understand—well— course they would understand if they thought about it. I don't believe they've thought about the implications of making peace with a vampire who will never die. [garbled] never die.
Wellby: I don't think you think they've thought about that? That seems like a significant thing to consider.
DM: Decisions in Ursk are not made in the way you think they might be made in other places. There is consensus always. It is not reached from lengthy deliberation and discussion.
DM: It is reached because there is a pecking order. Those at the top dictate the consensus. Do not wish Kinzal to dictate the consensus that we turn our western border over to this vampire.
Riswynn: We can only be in this place for a very short time. We're talking about completely restructuring your country. I'm talking—
DM: About you killing a vampire.

Riswynn: You want to give us a different quest than our proposed? Please sneak through the frost world, come out in the vampire world, kill the vampire, come back without having resurrected the leader.
DM: You have teleportation magic available to you?
DM: You do this, you must leave in the next 10 min. Why is that? Teleport out of this place and to the outskirts of the vampire's kingdom.

DM: I will understand if this is not what you wish. You have a simple path to your goals in front of you. Well— perhaps not so simple it involves traveling through the Frostfell and, resurrecting a dead man consumed by elemental fire. But you have a path before you. I know it is a risk for you to trust that I can help you.

Wellby: Here's the question. I actually, I love the idea of going and killing this vampire, that this is a— this sounds excellent to me. It's, but— we don't know that you can deliver on what you're saying.

Wellby: We don't even know that if we kill the vampire, then, you don't need control of the Rodnya. It doesn't matter whether or not the bloodline is resurrected, and even if you had control, if there's a pecking order, it doesn't seem like you could compel the other side. What—
Wellby: It's not just a risk you're asking us to take. A risk implies some knowledge of the odds. This seems like blind faith.
Delwath: There are some missing steps here, too. We kill the vampire and then return— Meet you somewhere. Mysterious?
Wellby: I mean we could resurrect him and then kill the vampire. After.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
Delwath: Outside exactly at— But, I'm curious as to answer to the question. And then what?
DM: 2 things. There are many among the Rodnya Voknaz who have taken this leader... This opportunity to grow strong, and we are prepared.
DM: We are ready if you bring back tokens of the vampire.
DM: He was once one of the Eyes of Vedmakov. There were once 9 Rodnya.
Riswynn: So the scandal will unsettle your government.
DM: Most of the other Rodnya would prefer this threat were eliminated.
DM: I know I'm asking you to trust me, and there is little I can do to prove that I can deliver on what I say.
Kenzo: Who are you? Give us something. Why should we trust you?
DM: Think. Think about what I know. You told anybody what your quest was?
DM: Told anybody about your conversation with Branek?
Seeker: You're the scribe— in— or someone who read the scribe's notes.
Kenzo: Do you know our quest?
DM: Knew what your quest was. Go to the Frostfell and resurrect the— a former, misguided, dangerous, tinkering with things that should not be tinkered with, head of this order.
Seeker: Are you a Eyes of Vedmakov? Is it easy?
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))

Delwath: 2 questions. So, we would just walk back into this place and knock on the door with the tokens from this vampire. That seems to be what you're implying. And why would we not just be imprisoned?
DM: Everything goes according to plan, I will be waiting to greet you. I will give you this. And he goes and reaches into his his—
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
DM: And takes something out and puts it down. And you see what materializes: little vial.
DM: He's clearly like hesitating whether he should mention this. It looks almost like a vial. It's like a vial of powdered stone.

DM: Of course you must know that all of the Rodnya locations are warded against teleportation and infiltration, but we must also be able to reach the inner sanctum of our— way one does it: teleportation magic, and stone from the inside of the castle.

DM: I am trusting you by giving you this. I'm trusting you not to just use this teleportation magic you claim to have, go steal what you're after, and leave all of us to scramble in the aftermath. But I am giving this to you as an assurance. If I fail, at least you have a way to get what you came.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))

DM: Okay, this guy is like super, he’s— or girl, but presumably it is the scribe, right, is super nervous. He's talking fast. He's like clearly like trying hard to convince you. He seems desperate. But he doesn't seem— there's nothing about him that seems what's the word, untrue, like he is—

DM: Right. He's like scrambling to convince you in a way that, like he realizes he's not, you know, he doesn't have— He's asking a lot of trust right? But he's basically scrambling to convince you to meddle in Urskan politics for him.

Riswynn: In politics, I mean, this is what I thought our quest was gonna be, is we're a scrappy little outside house, help us take on some neighboring menace to show that we're strong, and then the other houses will line behind us, and we'll become prominent. And this first guy was like, bring back my mentor, he's cool. I don't. I wasn't at all impressed with the first quest offered. So I love—
Seeker: Honestly like an alliance with vampires is just not a great idea. I think we could. We could help shut that down. Yeah.

Riswynn: Yeah. And this guy, the first guy didn't say, help bring back my mentor so that we can prevent an alliance with vampires or so that we can do good things for the little people, or you know the he just said, bring back my mentor because I like the status quo when I miss it.
Seeker: What was the thing about tokens? I didn't understand that part?

DM: He explained—I didn't explain it, but he would have explained it—the, so the vampire was once one of the watchers who used to be the ninth Rodnya. And when he betrayed them they were stripped of their bloodline. But he still bears the vampire— bound to his coffin, and the key to his like resurrection, vampire resurrection ability is one of the original symbols of the—
Delwath: So we could prove we killed him because—
DM: So you bring back that original—
DM: Symbol of the Eyes of Vedmakov. Then vampire can't regenerate and you prove he's dead.
Delwath: Again, wh—why does, why do we have to do this like, why can't we go in 4 h? What's gonna happen in the next 5 min?
Riswynn: The 10 min thing is a little bit up— Agree.

DM: Perhaps a few hours is not a problem, before you speak to Branek in the morning. You will not have the opportunity to vanish after that. Or Ludmila comes to wake you for breakfast. You must be gone.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
DM: The implication is like, once you meet with the guy, you're gonna be around Branek until you step through the portal.
Delwath: Yeah. But then, can't we just— mean, we have ways we could get back here.

DM: Well, this guy doesn't know that. He thinks once you step into the portal you're stuck until you resurrect. You could tell him that. That's—but that's the reason why he's telling you you've gotta leave soon, is that once you meet for breakfast you will be escorted until you step into the portal, and then you'll be stuck there until you resurrect the mage.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
Wellby: If we teleport into the vampire kingdom, how do we know where we're going, and how to find him, and how to kill him? And on and on.
Wellby: Do you have a map for us, or—
DM: Quick map of what we know. Yes.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
DM: I can draw you a map to reach the vampire's cap—to reach App— Rhodar von Glauer's capital easily. If you have teleportation magic. I believe you can get close.
Seeker: It's risky, I think, but doable.
DM: You need a safer passage. Wouldn't item help? An item from the location you need to teleport to, I believe makes it easier, yes?
DM: Hmm! Wonder how— this— cannot get you quite castle,
DM: But I can give you some dirt from the western border of Ursk. I would get you at least halfway there.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))
Seeker: I I think we should try to get as close to the castle itself.
Wellby: Like, huddle up? Are, are we doing this?
Wellby: Destabilizing governments is kind of our thing, but like is that—

Delwath: One last question for this guy? Like, why, why does he think his plan will work? Like, can you give us any hint but why he thinks this plan will actually work? Like, I'm all for killing a vampire, right, and honestly giving us the way to secretly teleport into the inner sanctum and steal the jade makes me feel better about trusting him, cause if he fails like— we could still—
Seeker: So just do that part. First, we—
Delwath: Also, he's clearly trusting us, cause we could just do that.
((Identity and language asides, checks, repetition, and teleportation tactics))

DM: I, I mean, you definitely get the sense that he, you know, he's not giving you a straight answer to why this is gonna work because he's desperate. But, you know, you basically pick up the—you get the following from sort of pressing a little bit. One is that. So the sort of the the history of like of Urskan politics was that you know, long ago, though you know it was like this.

DM: Morozmir was really the dominant Rodnya. They're the ones who developed this arcane ward that protects the cities of Ursk. But after the great, you know, after a while, like they, you know, things were—things stabilized and there was a long period of time when everybody was just kinda happy and got along.

DM: But in the past 20 years or so, maybe 30 years, Morozmir has grown reclusive and weird and dedicated ever more to these like esoteric rites, and that's left something of a power vacuum in Ursk, and the 2 Rodnya, and that were the strongest and prepared to fill it are Voknaz and Kinzal.

DM: And, Voknaz has always been the, the best defense is a good offense. They're on the West, so they've always hated the idea of just leaving the vampire. You know, a vampire kingdom, especially a vampire, who presumably has at least some magic just sitting there, and have always pushed, and this guy's sense, although again you just have to trust him is whether that's true or not is that that was the more popular opinion. And he is convinced that the other Rodnya were prepared to back a war to the West until this disaster.
DM: The whole mess up with the dragon, where the— leader of—he also believes that the leader of Voknaz was too arrogant and didn't want to ask for help and was trying—

DM: He, the the previous leader, the guy who's burning up with elemental fire, was like doing all sorts of crazy, esoteric research. Maybe a little too similar to Seeker, right? He wanted to find the one spell that would just be like, vampire dead. Don't ask for help, don't ally yourself with a whole bunch of other, Rodnya. Just. Find the spell that you can cast, and then the vampire dies, and then everybody loves that, obviously.
DM: So that's one piece of evidence. He's convinced that the other Rodnya would have supported a war and only didn't, because Voknaz screwed up the fight against the dragon.
DM: So he thinks that if that if he comes back with with the vampire dead that will tip the balance quite significantly. He also— Clearly—

DM: There's an opportunity somebody else can claim leadership of—I mean, there's Voknaz is in this sort of state of of kind of hibernation, almost, leaderless. But somebody could claim leadership. I mean, he won't tell you how that happens. But that's what he's clearly planning, is basically he says that there's people who are ready to claim the mantle of leadership of this Rodnya and the combination of that—

DM: But but who won't— Well, Kinzal is dominant because it because— or exactly the problem that if somebody if the, if Kinzal succeeds in their negotiations with the vampire, and says, we've made peace, and so, and Rodnya Voknaz, which is now seen as weak, you know, upends their leadership and claims they want war. They're worried that they'll just be decapitated, decapitated, and turn into the Watchers.
DM: Now, again, this is his perspective on Urskan politics. So, you know, everything DM says doesn't have to be true. It's from the perspective of this one NPC.

DM: But this is what, what he's trying to convince you of, is look, if I could just— if, if the vampire were dead, if it was fait accompli, that undercuts Kinzal, and makes Voknaz look strong and most of the Rodnya happier with that state of affairs.
Delwath: Gonna take credit? Is, are we supposed to, is, is—

DM: But yes, yes, yes, he is gonna take credit, but completely unwilling to actually have anybody associated with Voknaz attempt this mission, because if they fail, that would be the end of the Rodnya.
Kenzo: Wait. So if we succeed, then, what happens? They, they—
DM: If everything goes according to his plan, you come back with with these this Watcher symbol, symbol of the vampire.
DM: He's already carried out the coup and claimed leadership of Rodnya Voknaz, he gives you the jade.
DM: And then he marches to the other Rodnya, and says: Look, the new leadership of Voknaz has killed the vampire.
DM: This better than negotiating with? Isn't this better than negotiation? You should trust us. We're back. That's what he imagines.

Riswynn: And the philosophers basically were looking for something like this to happen, like I got, like we, the original intel that we got from the informational letter was like, Rodnya needs a big show of strength.

DM: So he gives you all this, and this conversation is, you know, been half an hour or something now, and he says: I cannot linger much longer. I leave you these. He left the 2 vials. And I— unless you have any more questions for him, he's about to vanish and say—
DM: I wish to see Ursk prosper.
Wellby: Why, why do you speak Drankorian?
DM: Wizards must learn all sorts of strange languages, and I might say, scribes are often called to translate as well.
DM: Leave you with these 2 teleportation tokens, and I hope that you are gone in the morning. You are gone, I will know. But, I know I ask a lot, and I will leave you to deliberate.
DM: If you wish to do so without risk of eavesdropping, have any magic? Believe I can mask the casting of one spell.
Delwath: Cast your—past your telepathy spell there.
DM: And with that he vanishes, leaving you to make your decision before everybody goes to bed, so I know which adventure I'm writing for tomorrow. Next time.

before: Kenzo: Alright!

after: Seeker: I— I was already thinking, starting to think of our ice vessel floating on top of the Magic Carpet is kind of like VW bus shaped, basically, like, kind of hollow ice submarine.

Kenzo: I I mean—

lines: Kenzo: Oh, so if we resurrect the dude, there's gonna be a peace treaty with the vampires. That's, that's, that's the deal. Oh, fuck that shit. Then let's go fucking kill the vampires. We can't let it, we can't let there be a peace treaty between Ursk and the vampires.
